name: sentryfeed
description: Self-hosted threat-intel dashboard on a Raspberry Pi: security news with CVE lookups, CISA exploitation flags, and colour-coded severity.

paragraphs: A threat-intel site at It began on a Raspberry Pi 3B at home and now runs on Vercel, with its database on Turso and its collector on GitHub Actions (see Setup); the Pi retired on 12 Oct 2026. Every 30 minutes it pulls security and tech news, looks up the CVEs each story mentions, checks whether CISA has confirmed they're being exploited, and colours every story by how much it matters. The front page reads like a newspaper: what matters today in one sentence, the most important stories, then sections for exploited flaws, the Gulf, markets and the week.
The same story from several outlets is shown once, with the other outlets listed under it.

requirements.text: Using it in a paid product or service would need Ransomware.live's written permission.

Tested with attacks on safefetch.py against real local test servers (107 checks: every blocked address range, 30 kinds of bad link, redirects to the metadata address, a private address, a login, another port and file:, endless redirects, a server that drips headers or body one byte at a time or goes silent after its headers, a 2 MB answer, and a DNS rebinding attempt), the…
There's deliberately no admin page yet, so there's no login to attack.
